hypothesis: The 16-18x high-eccentricity transfer gap was a limit of the training range, not a non-physical shortcut: a model trained on e in [0, 0.8] predicts held-out high-e systems (e in [0.5, 0.8], different data seed) nearly as well as low-e systems
expected_if_true: In both seeds, the held-out high_eccentricity val_mse_ratio is within 3x of the in-distribution val_mse_ratio, and the force and accel_step probes still beat their random controls by >= 0.1 at the final checkpoint
expected_if_false: The held-out high_eccentricity val_mse_ratio stays > 10x the in-distribution ratio even when high e is covered in training, which points to a shortcut that degrades at high e rather than a coverage gap
